evidence.quote: THE  PEOPLE OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK, REPRESENTED IN SENATE AND ASSEMBLY, DO ENACT AS FOLLOWS:

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Amends New York Penal Law § 245.15 so that unlawful dissemination or publication of an intimate image covers images created or altered by digitization, defined as altering an image in a realistic manner using images of another person or computer-generated images. Also repeals subdivision 2-a. Takes effect on the sixtieth day after enactment.
summary.long: Section 1 amends penal law section 245.15 subdivisions 1 and 2, added by chapter 109 of the laws of 2019. Subdivision 1(a) keeps the offence of intentionally disseminating or publishing a still or video image showing another person with intimate parts exposed or engaging in sexual conduct, with intent to cause harm to emotional, financial or physical welfare, and now expressly includes an image created or altered by digitization where the person is reasonably identifiable. Subdivision 1(b) requires that the actor knew or reasonably should have known the person did not consent, including for an image first taken with consent where the depicted person had a reasonable expectation that it would remain private. Subdivision 2 adds a definition of digitization and keeps definitions of intimate part, and refers to other provisions for disseminate, publish and sexual conduct. Section 2 repeals subdivision 2-a, whose content the bill does not reproduce. Section 3 sets the effective date as the sixtieth day after the act becomes law. The bill states no penalty; the offence sits within the penal law.

obligations.summary: A person may not intentionally disseminate or publish an intimate or sexually explicit image of another person, including an image created or altered by digitization, with intent to cause harm, where the actor knew or reasonably should have known the depicted person did not consent. Section 1 amends the offence to add digitized images and consent language.
obligations.applies_from: sixtieth day after the act becomes law (Section 3)
obligations.conditional_on: intent to cause harm; depicted person identifiable; actor knew or reasonably should have known of lack of consent

evidence.quote: they intentionally disseminate or publish a still or video image depicting such other person with one or more intimate parts exposed or engaging in sexual conduct with another person

entities.note: The bill names no firms, facilities or public bodies and designates or empowers no authority; it addresses 'a person' generically.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changes legal treatment. The only number (the sixtieth day after enactment, § 3) sets the effective date and is a procedural time limit, not a threshold.

enforcement.note: Section 1 amends Penal Law § 245.15(1) to define the offence of unlawful dissemination or publication of an intimate image ('is guilty of'), but the text states no penalty, sentence, fine, authority or cure period. Section 2 repeals subdivision 2-a and section 3 sets the effective date. The penalty grade is not stated in this text.
